fixes.explanation: It's a fair guess, friend. That's a big ask, and most of us would have questions ready. But the text doesn't show Hosea pushing back at all. It says, "So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim…" (Hosea 1:3) It just tells us he went.

That's right, friend. The text shows Hosea going, not pushing back. It says, "So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim…" (Hosea 1:3) It doesn't record a single word of argument from him, and I won't make one up either.

That's it, baker. The LORD says, "…I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel." (Hosea 1:4) Jeroboam was Israel's king when this word came. Bloodshed on the house of Jehu, and an end to the kingdom. Both are in the same verse.

Judah is in this passage too, friend, but not for this. The LORD says, "…I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel." (Hosea 1:4) And hang onto Judah, because the LORD has something different to say about it a few verses later.
Moab never comes up in this passage, friend. The LORD says, "…I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel." (Hosea 1:4) That word is about Israel, and Moab isn't in it.
Good thinking, friend, but the LORD never mentions Samaria or its walls here. He says, "…I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel." (Hosea 1:5) It's a bow He breaks, not a wall.

Egypt is a good guess for a sneaky backup plan, friend, but it never comes up here. The LORD says He'll save them "…not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God." (Hosea 1:7) The LORD their God is the one who saves them.
